post.originalText:
This is what a robot dog sees.

I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to give my robot dog a lidar, two depth cameras and a brain that walks it in a physics sim. 

It took 8h and $94.32 in API cost with Opus 5.5 on medium. https://t.co/X327qHmuvI

sourceMaterials.text:
Claude Opus 5.5 wrote all of it
CAD: build123d, 625 parts, 29 kg
Physics: MuJoCo, convex MPC trot controller, 80 N m motors
Perception: simulated Mid-360 + 2x D435i, elevation map, person tracking
Planning: A*, MPPI, footstep scoring
Film: three.js, real HDRI light, procedural music
sourceMaterials.author: konstantinsaifo

sourceMaterials.text:
Every step: 121 candidate footholds scored on the map for edges, slope, roughness and reach.
The knee folds backward, so the shin needs room behind the foot or it hits the step nose. Opus found that one in its own tests.

The panel bottom right is the controller live: which feet touch the ground (straight from the physics contacts), body height and pitch. It pitches up to 27 degrees on the stairs.
sourceMaterials.author: konstantinsaifo

sourceMaterials.text:
Konstantin Saifoulline on X: "A 2.5D elevation map, 4 cm cells, fused from lidar and depth. A* over that map for the route, about 20 to 30 ms in Python on a laptop.

MPPI on top: 512 possible futures, 2 s each, 10 times a second. It tracks the person, predicts where they walk and steers around." / X
